name: Ginger
perishability: Semi-perishable. Fresh rhizomes keep 1–3 months; dried ginger keeps a year.
summary: Sold fresh as a kitchen staple and dried as a spice. It is planted before the monsoon and dug from October onwards, mostly by smallholders in the hills and plateaus of the South and North-East. Like garlic it runs in multi-year boom–bust cycles: ₹10/kg in 2021, ₹250–400/kg in mid-2023, then a collapse again.

key_numbers.label: World rank
key_numbers.note: India is the largest ginger producer

global: India grows the most ginger in the world and exports fresh and dried ginger to Bangladesh, the Gulf, Europe and the US. 'Cochin' and 'Calicut' dried ginger are long-standing export grades.

states.basis: Major producing states (not ranked; reported shares vary a lot by year)

belts.name: Malnad
belts.note: Largest commercial belt; many Kerala growers lease land here.

belts.name: North-East hills
belts.note: Large area of low-input, often organic ginger; long haul to markets.

seasons.name: Main crop
seasons.note: Planted with pre-monsoon showers. Green ginger from 6 months (Oct); mature ginger for drying and storage at 8–10 months (Dec–Mar).

lean_season: June–September, before the new crop, when old stock is thin.

climate.v: Warm and humid, 19–28 °C; tolerates partial shade.
1,500–3,000 mm, or irrigation; a dry spell before harvest helps.
Loose, well-drained loam rich in organic matter, pH 5.5–6.5; waterlogging spreads soft rot.

weather_risks.impact: Soft rot and bacterial wilt spread through fields.

pests.name: Soft rot (rhizome rot)
pests.impact: The most damaging disease; spreads with water and infected seed rhizomes.

pests.name: Bacterial wilt
pests.impact: Rapid wilting; no cure once in field.

postharvest.storage: Fresh: 12–14 °C, 65–70% RH. Seed rhizomes: pits lined with sawdust or sand.
practices: Washed and air-dried before bagging for fresh trade.
Dried ginger is peeled and sun-dried (about 16–25% of fresh weight).
Seed rhizomes are a large share of cost; growers keep part of the crop as seed.

steps.what: Dug by hand; many farmers sell standing crop to traders.
Shivamogga, Hassan, Guwahati and Aurangabad markets.
Fresh retail, paste makers, dried ginger and oleoresin units.

supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

trade.exports: Fresh and dried ginger to Bangladesh, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Netherlands, UK, US.
trade.imports: Some from Nepal and Myanmar during shortages.

policy.what: Spices Board promotes dried ginger exports; no MSP.

history.what: Farm prices of ₹10–15/kg; growers in Karnataka faced heavy losses.
Retail ₹250–400/kg after reduced planting and rot losses.
Area expanded after 2023; prices fell back.

signals: Planting area in Karnataka and the North-East in Apr–Jun.
Monsoon rainfall and soft-rot reports in Jul–Sep.
Arrivals in Bengaluru and Azadpur from October.
business: Ginger-garlic paste is a large processed category; paste makers buy heavily in gluts.
Prices run in multi-year cycles; contracts with seed and price support help growers stay in through busts.
North-East organic ginger is under-marketed relative to its quality.
